challenge.reason: The supersession argument is sound. The old decision rested on two stated premises: runs under 20 issues and single-writer simplicity. Both are now false: runs admit 200+ issues and the concurrency executor writes many issues in parallel. The new design addresses the two concrete failures that follow from that change (one lock serialising every heartbeat and status write, and one corrupt byte losing the whole run's state), keeps the same directory root, and adds an index file so existing discovery still works. Residual risk to verify at build time: the index file and the per-issue files can disagree after a partial write, so the index update needs its own atomic write and a recovery rule. That is an implementation detail, not a flaw in the supersession argument.
